body.p: In the Office Action mailed on February 15, 2023, claims 1-13 are pending in the application; Claims 1-7 and 11-12 are withdrawn; Claims 8-10 and 13 stand rejected.
As set forth herein, reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections and objections of the claims is respectfully requested.

The Examiner objected to the disclosure of the prior-filed application provisional application (60/990,834) as failing to provide adequate support or enablement for claim 8 that recites "a wireless electronic digital stethoscope," "polling command from the stethoscope," and "weigh scale,". The Examiner also objected to claim 13 for reciting "a wireless electronic digital stethoscope," and "weigh scale".

The Examiner further objected to claim 8 for reciting a "polling command from the stethoscope," and "weigh scale," that are not disclosed in the Application No. 12/267,448. Similarly, the Examiner objected to claim 13 for reciting a "weigh scale,"
The Examiner further objected to recitation in Claim 8 of the "polling command from the stethoscope," as not being disclosed in the parent application, Application No. 13/442,569.

This application is a divisional application of Application No. 13/442,569 (US Patent No. 11,3890,080), which is a continuation in part of Application No. 12/267,448 (US Patent No. 8,152,734). This application also claim priority to the provisional application (60/990,834).

The term "polling command" is deleted from the claims in favor of the term "query" which finds support in the specification as recognized by the Examiner. The term "weight scale" is deleted from the claims. The term "wireless electronic digital stethoscope" in the claims is replaced with "stethoscope". Page 4, lines 13-15 of the prior filed provisional application (60/990,834) recites "Collection of lung sounds is preferably obtained by a digital/electronic stethoscope that is capable of expressing sounds in the form of a spectrogram." The amended pending claims have adequate support from the prior-filed provisional application (60/990,834). Therefore, the Examiner's conclusion as to priority should be reconsidered and withdrawn in light of the amendments to claims 8 and 13.

The Examiner objected to the specification as failing to provide proper antecedent basis for the claimed "polling" operation. The claimed "polling" is deleted from the claims and therefore this objection should be withdrawn.

Claims 8-10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, as failing to comply with the written description requirement. The Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.
The Examiner rejected the claims based on the "polling command" which has been deleted from the claims. Therefore, this rejection should be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Claims 8-10 and 13 are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over US Patent Publication No. 2006/0201432 (hereinafter referred as Pratt) in view of US Patent Publication No. 2007/0106179 (hereinafter referred as Bagha) further in view of US Patent Publication No. 2004/0236241) (hereinafter referred as Murphy). The Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

Claim 8 is amended to further recite wherein the value is a numerical lung score compared to threshold values that correspond to respiratory conditions indicating the health status of the animal's respiratory condition expressed in a scaled lung score. Original claim 13 recites the same wherein clause. The scaled lung score is obtained from the calculated numerical lung score being compared to known respiratory conditions that relate to the health status of the animal. Even if Pratt, Bagha and Murphy are properly combinable under Section 103(a), the combined teachings of these references do not remotely disclose the subject matter of the aforementioned wherein clause. The Examiner concludes that Murphy at [0081] teaches the content of this wherein clause. The paragraph [0081] in Murphy does not describe anything relating to the characterization of lung sounds to determine a health status but rather, this paragraph simply explains how discrete sound artifacts (i.e. noise) is distinguished from "adventitious" sounds (i.e. the targeted sounds from the respiration of the animal). An example slope threshold constant is identified in Murphy (.015) in which the median of the preliminary threshold trace is multiplied by this constant. The resulting value is then added to the preliminary threshold trace to form a slope threshold trace. Next,

following the process described with respect to Figs. 8 and 9A and 9B (see [0082-0090]), it is clear that the identification of noise is necessary to obtain measurable sound data from the animal's respiration as opposed to a mixed signal that includes both noise and respiration sounds. Thus, it is clear that what the Examiner references in Murphy has no relation to the aforementioned wherein clause because Murphy does not teach any form of a numerical lung score compared to threshold values that corresponds to respiratory conditions indicating the health status of the animal's respiratory condition. Further, Murphy does not remotely disclose a respiratory condition that is expressed as a scaled lung score. The process of separating undesirable noise from targeted sounds of respiration in Murphy cannot be deemed equivalent to the subject matter of the claimed wherein clause. Pratt and Bahga fail to cure the deficiencies in Murphy. Therefore, this rejection should be reconsidered and withdrawn.
Based on the foregoing, Applicant believes all pending claims are in condition for allowance and such disposition is respectfully requested.
RESPECTFULLY SUBMITTED, BERG HILL GREENLEAF RUSCITTI LLP
